**ID:** Snp 5.13 (PTS Snp 213)

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhadrāvudhamāṇavapucchā* is the thirteenth discourse in the *Pārāyanavagga*, the fifth chapter of the *Suttanipāta* (verses 1101–1104, PTS p. 213) [Anderson & Smith 1913; Norman 1997–2001; Hazra 1994]. In this dialogue, the student Bhadrāvudha approaches the Buddha and asks how he came to know the Dhamma. The Buddha instructs him that a monk must not grasp after anything in the world, for whenever one grasps after worldly things, Māra follows [Hazra 1994].
